data.description: Gold prices are poised for their second consecutive weekly decline, driven by the strengthening US dollar and escalating Treasury yields. Investors are keenly anticipating vital US payroll figures that could sway the Federal Reserve's future policy decisions. Current predictions suggest only a 25% probability of a rate increase this month, which is a shift from previous projections.

			  "articleBody":"Gold prices fell on Friday and were on track for a second straight weekly decline, pressured by a firmer US dollar and elevated Treasury yields, while investors awaited key US payrolls data for clues on the Federal Reserve's policy path.Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,154.78 per ounce by 0205 GMT and was down more than 3% for the week so far. US gold futures lost 0.4% to $4,184.00.The US dollar was headed for a weekly gain, making greenback-priced metals more expensive for holders of other currencies, while yields on 10- and 30-year Treasuries hit their highest levels since 2002 on Thursday. [USD/] [US/] Market participants are watching US interest rate expectations and geopolitical developments in the Middle East,  said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. US nonfarm payroll data will be critical for rate expectations. If it comes in hot, it may increase the chances of rate hikes from the Fed. That would potentially weigh even further on gold prices. metadata.description: Gold prices are poised for their second consecutive weekly decline, driven by the strengthening US dollar and escalating Treasury yields. Investors are keenly anticipating vital US payroll figures that could sway the Federal Reserve's future policy decisions. Current predictions suggest only a 25% probability of a rate increase this month, which is a shift from previous projections.
